chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyr, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a slave who slandered a free person. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is whipped eighty [lashes]. This is from the rights of the people. So as for what is from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then he is whipped half the penalty (Hadd).' I said, 'What is that which is from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he commits adultery or drinks wine, then these are from the rights for which he is whipped half the penalty (Hadd) with regards to it.'

key_terms.قَذَفَ: To slander or accuse of adultery

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for a slave versus a free person regarding slander and adultery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction in penal codes between 'Huquq al-Nas' (rights of people), where slaves receive the full eighty lashes for slander, and 'Huquq Allah' (rights of God), where penalties for adultery or intoxication are halved to forty lashes. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly consensus on the proportional reduction of corporal punishment for slaves, emphasizing that the nature of the offense dictates the severity of the penalty rather than a uniform reduction across all categories.
